The venture unraveled when financial pressures exposed discrepancies between its public narrative and its actual operations. In May 2025, Builder.ai collapsed into insolvency after lender Viola Credit seized $37 million from its accounts over breached loan terms, leaving the company with approximately $5 million. The seizure followed reporting by Bloomberg alleging the startup inflated revenue between 2021 and 2024 through round-tripping—exchanging reciprocal invoices with Indian company VerSe [...] ⁠  
Key aspects of the fallout remain contested. VerSe Innovation and its leadership have strongly denied participating in round-tripping, calling the allegations baseless and defamatory. In addition, while U.S. federal prosecutors issued a subpoena for Builder.ai’s financial and customer records, no criminal charges have been confirmed in the available records, leaving the ultimate legal status of the inquiries open. [...] Behind Builder.ai’s promise of an automated artificial intelligence named Natasha was not autonomous code generation, but an estimated team of 700 human software developers in India manually assembling applications. Marketed as a no-code platform that built custom software cheaper and faster than traditional development, the company drew hundreds of millions of dollars from high-profile backers including Microsoft and the Qatar Investment Authority.⁠  
⁠

In May 2025, Builder.ai announced insolvency proceedings after creditors seized $50 million borrowed in October 2024. In response to the company's high debt and low cash balances, some shareholders provided $75 million to the company, with Duggal seeking a deal with investors to buy back the company. By June, the company had laid off 80% of its workforce, or around 1,000 people.

## See also

[edit] [...] Builder.ai (formerly Engineer.ai Corporation) was a smartphone application development company that claimed to use AI to massively speed up app development. The company was based mostly in the United Kingdom and the United States, with smaller subsidiaries in Singapore and India. After years of allegations that it had exaggerated its AI capabilities (instead relying on outsourced human contractors) and misreported its financials, the company entered insolvency proceedings in 2025.
